messages:
sanjay: Heads-up — we're seeing intermittent multi‑GPU hangs / AllReduce timeouts on the eu-west inference pool after yesterday's NCCL 2.22.3 + CUDA 12.1 driver push. Impacting a few high‑throughput LLM routes under steady load. :warning:

 tara: Ugh. Any pattern? specific instance types / NVLink vs PCIe?

 sanjay: Mostly A100s with NVLink enabled. Symptoms: progressive backlog on worker queues, then one rank hits a nccl timeout and the whole collective stalls for ~30–90s. Not single‑request latency spike but tails + dropped throughput. Happened on 3 different host revisions.

 alex: Deploy bot shows canary finished ~09:12 UTC on eu-west2. deploy-bot: canary deploy 2026-03-17T09:12 UTC, group: eu-west-inference, version: runtime-4.7.1, nccl:2.22.3, cuda:12.1, result: success (no health-check errors) :white_check_mark:

 mike: We've seen similar behavior last quarter when the kernel + driver interactions exposed a selective timeout in the transport layer. Did we get any IB/RDMA error logs?

 sanjay: Pulling logs. Example from worker-17: ```
[2026-03-17 09:14:02] worker-17 nccl INFO starting ring
[2026-03-17 09:14:31] worker-17 nccl WARN AllReduce timed out rank 2 -> rank 0
[2026-03-17 09:14:31] worker-17 kernel: NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 79, GPU has fallen off the bus
[2026-03-17 09:15:00] inference-worker supervisor: queue depth rising, not scheduling new inferences
```
Not every host shows NVRM Xid but the timing aligns with a collective stall.

 tara: Any correlation with autoscaler? If pods are contending for GPUs and preemption occurs, collectives can deadlock. What were pod densities on affected hosts?

 alex: Affected hosts had 3 high‑concurrency pods each (batching enabled). We bumped burst capacity yesterday to reduce queuing, so more co‑location than usual.

 mike: Quick triage actions I recommend: 1) pin the canary back to nccl 2.22.1 on eu-west 2) taint new nodes to stop scheduling high‑concurrency pods 3) enable NCCL_DEBUG=INFO on a small subset and capture traces 4) set NCCL_P2P_DISABLE=1 as an experiment to see if P2P is the culprit.

 sanjay: Agree. I'm starting a rollback on the canary now for eu-west. If rollback isn't immediate we should at least reduce co‑location density — tainting and draining low‑priority pods.

 deploy-bot: rollback job started for group eu-west-inference -> target runtime-4.6.9 (nccl 2.22.1, cuda 12.0.1). ETA ~12m.

 tara: Also try setting NCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME to the Mellanox interface and disable IB_GID if there are GID index mismatches: `export NCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME=eth0; export NCCL_IB_DISABLE=1` — that'll force TCP fallback but is quick to test.

 mike: If TCP fallback removes the hangs, it's a strong signal the IB/RDMA path in 2.22.3+12.1 combo regressed. We'll need to open a ticket with NVIDIA/NCCL with collected nccl-traces.

 sanjay: Rolling out the taint + drain to 4 hosts now, and enabling NCCL_DEBUG capture on 2 replicas. Also increasing autoscaler headroom to avoid tight packing.

 alex: What about cost/latency tradeoffs? If we force TCP fallback or reduce co‑location we'll pay higher unit cost or increased latency. Do we have a short term SLA plan for key customers?

 tara: For the short term we pin critical routes to dedicated instances (no co‑location) — higher cost but avoids regressions. Ops: mark these routes as 'critical' in traffic router.

 ops-bot: route flag update: /llm-generation -> priority:critical, pinned_pool:eu-west-dedicated-1. Changes applied.

 mike: OK. If rollback resolves the issue, we should do a controlled re‑test: deploy 2.22.3 to a small isolated pool with synthetic load that matches our 99th percentile sequence lengths and measure collective stability for 24h. If instability reproduces, escalate to vendor.

 sanjay: Rollback completed to 2.22.1 on canary group at 09:38 UTC. Early signs: queue depth dropping on previously hot hosts. I'll keep the debug traces until we confirm.

 tara: Nice. File a postmortem + RCA once we have traces. For now set a hold on NCCL 2.22.3 on all inference pools.

 mike: I'll open the vendor ticket and attach nccl traces + kernel logs + host configs (BIOS, NVLink firmware, driver).

 sanjay: Thanks team — continue monitoring; if anyone sees a recurrence after rollback ping me directly. :eyes:
